title: Contrastive golden playback for quantization acceptance
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement an automated acceptance harness that runs contrastive playback of golden prompts across FP32 baseline, FP8 candidate, and INT8 candidate variants. The harness will produce per-prompt pass/fail signals using a combination of contrastive metrics (embedding cosine delta, token-level KL, and rank-recall on reference outputs) and a weighted cohort gating policy. This ticket covers the automation, CI integration, telemetry, and initial threshold tuning for canary rollouts of quantized profiles.
acceptance_criteria: 1) CI job that replays golden corpus against baseline FP32, FP8, and INT8 runs completes in < 45m for 10k prompts. 2) For each prompt cohort, compute: embedding cosine delta, token-KL, and top-k answer rank recall. 3) Gate decision algorithm returns PASS/FLAG/FAIL according to configurable thresholds and cohort weights. 4) Dashboard displays per-prompt delta distributions, flaky-prompt list, and historical trend. 5) Alerts fire to #runtime-quant on FAIL or trend regression > 1.5x baseline variance.
implementation_steps: 1) Curate initial golden set and cohort metadata; add adversarial perturbation generator. 2) Implement runner that streams candidate outputs into scoring service; ensure deterministic seeds. 3) Compute contrastive metrics: embedding cosine (use embed-service v2), token-level KL normalized by length, rank recall against golden answers. 4) Build gating policy engine that supports weighted cohorts and per-metric thresholds. 5) Add CI pipeline (github actions) and flaky-prompt detector that quarantines noisy prompts. 6) Wire telemetry to Console dashboard and create alerting rules. 7) Run smoke run and weight-tune thresholds with PM/Research feedback.

decisions: Use contrastive approach (delta vs baseline) rather than absolute thresholds to reduce false positives on stable model shifts.
Combine three orthogonal metrics (embedding cosine delta, token-KL, rank-recall) into a weighted score. Initial weights: embed 0.5, KL 0.3, recall 0.2.
Run canonical FP32 baseline at fixed temperature and deterministic RNG to make deltas comparable.
Quarantine prompts with high variance across runs (stddev normalized > 0.2) and surface them as flaky for manual review before gating decisions.
Integrate acceptance harness into PR gating for quant profile branches but allow override by runtime SRE for emergency rollbacks.
Score thresholds initially tuned on historical datasets; thresholds to be re-evaluated after three canary rollouts.
Prefer embedding service for semantic deltas over BLEU-like string metrics to better capture LLM semantics.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Golden set may not represent customer distribution -> Mitigation: include stratified cohorts from production traffic and schedule periodic golden refreshes.
Risk: Flaky prompts generate false FAILs -> Mitigation: quarantine noisy prompts and maintain a stable-approved list for gating.
Risk: CI runtime cost too high for regular gating -> Mitigation: incremental sampling and stratified downsampling for nightlies, full run for release gates.
Risk: Embedding service latency affects overall runtime -> Mitigation: batch embedding requests and use cached vectors for unchanged prompts.
Risk: Metric weights misaligned with perceived quality -> Mitigation: PM/Research validation sessions and A/B comparisons against human judgments.
Risk: Overfitting thresholds to historical anomalies -> Mitigation: use rolling windows and conservative initial gates; enable manual override with audit trail.
Risk: Security/data exposure with production prompts -> Mitigation: strip PII, hash prompt IDs, and run private builds for sensitive cohorts in Private deployments.
Risk: Regression alerts noisy -> Mitigation: require sustained regression for 3 consecutive runs before paging on-call.
Risk: False sense of safety if only comparing to FP32 -> Mitigation: include multiple baselines and variant ensembles in extended runs.
next_steps: 1) Optimize IO and embedding batching to get full 10k run under 45m. 2) Finalize threshold tuning with Research using a labeled 2k held-out set. 3) Add canary CI job and hook into PR gating for quant-profile branches. 4) Run first canary rollout and collect telemetry for three consecutive cycles before formalizing gate thresholds.
notes: This approach emphasizes relative fidelity vs FP32 and is intended to reduce spurious rejections caused by innocuous generative variation. Follow-on work should explore probabilistic thresholds and model-agnostic golden sampling to avoid model-specific bias.
